title: Apparent Stillness
text:
Apparent stillness before your eyes,

here, this wound-there are no alien limits-,

today is the pointer of your stable balance.

The wound is yours, the body in which it opens

is yours, though stiff and livid. Come, touch,

come down, closer. Do you perhaps see your origin

entering through your eyes into this

contrary part of life? What have you found?

Anything that is not permanently yours?

Throw away your dagger. Throw away your senses.

Within you, what you have given begets you;

it was yours and is always continuous action.

This wound is witness: no one has died.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the wound as shared origin and testimony rather than a simple image of death.

title: Song
text:
It is not what is broken, no,

the water held by the glass:

what is broken is the glass,

and the water spills onto the floor.


It is not what is broken, no,

the light that holds the day:

what is broken is time,

and it slips into shadow.


It is not what is broken, no,

the blood that lifts you:

what is broken is your body,

and in dream you pour yourself out.


It is not what is broken, no,

the box of thought:

what is broken is the idea

that carries it toward pride.


It is not God who is broken,

nor the field He has created:

what is broken is the man

who does not see God in His field.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated correction: the container, body, idea, and human sight are broken, not the essence.

title: The Old Stoic
text:
I feel little esteem for riches,

and at Love I laugh with disdain.

The desire for fame was only a dream

that vanished with the dawn.


And, if I pray, the only prayer

that moves my lips is:

"Leave this heart I possess

and give me freedom!"


My days draw swiftly toward the end,

and that is all I implore.

In life and in death, an unchained soul,

with courage to resist.




1841
editorial_note: The translation follows the Spanish Brontë text and preserves the dated closing.

title: I Will Come to You
text:
I will come to you

when you are very sad,

in the solitude of the dark room,

when the cheerful, mad day has fled,

and the happy smile has been erased

by the sadness of the cold night.


I will come to you

when your heart's true feeling

reigns impartial and absolute,

and my silent influence,

pain deepened, joy frozen,

will rise without delay with your soul.


Listen! It is the hour,

the moment you so feared.

Do you not feel in your breast the flowing

of the river of a strange sensation,

forerunner of a stronger power

whose herald is me?
editorial_note: The translation keeps the visitation as a dark-room presence that arrives with sadness and power.

title: Soft Mist over the Hill
text:
Soft mist over the hill;

tomorrow there will be no storm.

No; the day has grown tired of weeping,

has already spent its store of silent sadness.


Oh, I have returned to the days of my childhood,

I am a child again;

and beneath the paternal roof that shelters me,

beside the old entrance door,


I watch this cloudy evening fall

after a rainy day.

Blue mists, sweet summer mists,

dim the mountains far away.


Moisture soaks the tall green grass,

thick as tears in the morning;

and breaths of fragrance pass as in dreams,

recalling other times.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the misty return to childhood and the rain-soaked sensory memory.
